_STATUS: REFERENCE ONLY. NOT READ AT RUNTIME. Editing this file changes NOTHING.
_why: ADR-4 made this file the single home for CRM specifics and had WF-2 read it
infra/docker-compose.yml. That was the abandoned VPS design. Production is
Railway, which has no bind mounts, and the n8n worker's /home/node/.n8n is
ephemeral. The file therefore NEVER existed in production, an empty catch
swallowed the miss, and delivered_api was false for every lead from
2026-07-22 to 2026-08-18 with nobody told. See DECISIONS 2026-08-18.
ADR-4's intent (one documented home for CRM specifics) is kept by this file.
ADR-4's mechanism (reading it at runtime) is superseded by env vars.

_runtime_config_lives_in.LEADSIMPLE_REST_KEY: secret. LeadSimple > Settings > Integrations > REST API
_runtime_config_lives_in._note: Queue mode: set every one on BOTH the n8n main AND worker services.

_contract_verified_live_2026-08-18.auth_note: A 'Bearer <key>' prefix also returns 200; the swagger declares a bare apiKey header, so we send the raw key.
_contract_verified_live_2026-08-18.success: 201 -> { data: { id, link, ... } }. A 2xx with no data.id is NOT treated as delivery.
_contract_verified_live_2026-08-18.documented_errors: 401 Errors::Authorization, 404 Errors::NotFound. No 400 is documented on POST /deals even though POST /webhook_subscriptions documents one, so how a bad field surfaces is UNVERIFIED.
_contract_verified_live_2026-08-18.rate_limits: Per ACCOUNT, not per key, 1-minute window. Observed 100 requests / 1000 records. Read X-RateLimit-Retry-After rather than assuming a fixed backoff.
_contract_verified_live_2026-08-18.spec_version: info.version 0.0.1 - young API, prove behaviour by running it
_contract_verified_live_2026-08-18.no_idempotency_key: POST /deals has no external_id or idempotency field.
CORRECTION_accept_duplicates: An earlier version of this file claimed deal[accept_duplicates]=false gives
server-side dedupe on email or phone. THAT IS WRONG. Measured live
2026-08-18: two POSTs with the same email produced two separate deals
(db4f8e27, 60e5a983) one second apart. They shared ONE contact
(4369952e) but got TWO property and TWO unit records. So the flag
dedupes the CONTACT, not the DEAL. Do not rely on it to prevent
duplicate leads. WF-2 carries its own guard instead.
CORRECTION_search_is_not_a_read_back: An earlier version claimed GET /deals?search=<email> is the read-back that
makes delivery provable. It is not, for TWO reasons measured live:
1. search on a FULL email returns 0 hits, always. The query breaks on the
'@'. The local part alone matches; the domain alone matched 14 deals.
2. search is an INDEX and it LAGS. A deal created seconds earlier was not
found by search, then was found 90s later. Immediately after a create:
The reliable read-backs are GET /deals/{id} using the id from the 201, and
which is a direct ordered query and is consistent immediately.
_contract_verified_live_2026-08-18.terminology: LeadSimple calls a lead a Deal. deal[pipeline_id] is the ONLY required field.

_write_shape_is_not_read_shape._note: Verified live 2026-08-18 on a created deal. Asserting the write-side names against a read response reports data loss that is not happening.
_write_shape_is_not_read_shape.property[num_bedrooms]: reads back as property.unit.num_bedrooms (as a string, e.g. "3.0")
_write_shape_is_not_read_shape.contact[full_name]: title-cased and split on separators: "jsmith-happy" becomes "Jsmith Happy". OMITTING IT makes LeadSimple invent the contact name "Unknown Name".

_field_map_real_names.phone: contact[phone_numbers][][kind] + contact[phone_numbers][][phone]  (array of objects, e.g. kind=mobile)
_field_map_real_names.full name: contact[full_name]  (LeadSimple parses it into first/last; unused, the form collects no name)

_useful_reads.read back one deal: GET /deals/{deal_id}  <- ALWAYS consistent, use the id from the 201
_useful_reads.read back a just-written deal: GET /pipelines/{id}/deals?per_page=25&order_field=created_at&order_direction=desc  <- consistent IMMEDIATELY, this is what the duplicate guard reads
_useful_reads.find a deal by email: DOES NOT WORK. GET /deals?search=<full email> returns 0 every time; the query breaks on the '@'. Search the local part instead, and only after the index catches up (~tens of seconds).
_useful_reads.webhooks: POST /webhook_subscriptions { event_name, target_url }; event enum includes deal/created
